sectors.name: Technology

Cloud and enterprise software adoption by Indonesian SMEs and corporates is accelerating, supported by rising digitization and foreign investment in data centers.
US tech rate sensitivity remains a structural headwind for Indonesia-listed tech stocks, given their correlation with global risk appetite and foreign portfolio flows.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector underperformed with a -1.15% drag, but selective catalysts like MCAS (+34.59%) and SAP (+9.26%) signal pockets of strength. Watch for US rate sensitivity and local digital adoption tailwinds; position tactically in high-momentum names while avoiding broad exposure until macro clarity improves.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable energy transition is structurally driven by the government's 23% renewable energy mix target by 2025, which creates a durable policy floor for solar and geothermal investments de

The Omnibus Law on Job Creation provides a long-term regulatory framework for foreign investment in renewables, reducing bureaucratic hurdles and enabling capital flows into climate-tech infrastructur
PLN's mandatory renewable energy procurement quotas for state-owned utilities are a structural demand driver, forcing grid integration of solar and wind capacity over the next decade.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector is underperforming global peers, but watch for policy catalysts from the upcoming Omnibus Law implementation and PLN's green energy procurement targets. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Premiumization in personal care and household products is driving margin expansion for niche players like AGAR and KLIN, as middle-class consumers trade up to branded essentials.
Food and beverage demand remains resilient, with TFCO and SOSS benefiting from distribution network expansion into tier-2 cities, capturing urbanization tailwinds.
Regulatory stability and subsidy rationalization in staples like cooking oil and sugar are creating predictable cost environments for FMCG firms, supporting earnings visibility.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector underperformed today, dragged by domestic names, but US strength signals resilience. Watch for selective bottom-fishing in high-momentum movers like AGAR and KLIN, which may indicate niche demand recovery. Maintain WATCH for broader rotation into staples as inflation moderates.

sectors.name: Logistics

Cold-chain logistics is underpenetrated in Indonesia's archipelago, with rising food and pharmaceutical compliance creating durable moats for early movers like BULL and TNCA.
sectors.ai: Indonesia logistics underperformed regional peers, dragged by macro headwinds, but select movers like BULL (+12.31%) and TNCA (+7.14%) signal niche demand for cold-chain and last-mile delivery. Watch for consolidation plays as e-commerce growth and infrastructure spending drive structural tailwinds for efficient logistics providers.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's young, mobile-first population drives structural crypto adoption as a hedge against rupiah depreciation and limited traditional investment options.
The government's dual-track approach—promoting blockchain innovation via the Digital Financial Innovation sandbox while tightening crypto tax compliance—creates persistent regulatory uncertainty.
Global institutional inflows into DeFi and tokenized assets, led by AAVE and ONDO, are amplifying local altcoin speculation, but Indonesia's fragmented exchange landscape limits liquidity depth.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's crypto rally is a high-beta play on global liquidity easing and local retail FOMO, but regulatory overhang from BI's CBDC push and potential tax tightening on crypto gains creates a binary risk. Watch for a pullback to re-enter; the sector's momentum is fragile without clear ID-specific catalysts.
